key_insight: Sb doping creates bright self-trapped excitons in Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals, while Na→K alloying tunes the exciton lattice distortion and shifts photoluminescence without strongly changing absorption.
engineering_relevance: Composition control in lead-free double perovskites offers a practical route to tune emission color and polarization response for optoelectronic and photocatalytic materials design.
method: Optical spectroscopy of Sb-doped Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals with B-site alloying from Na to K
Ab initio calculations of excitonic states, lattice distortion, and radiative recombination
Time-resolved polarization-anisotropy measurements to test wavefunction-dependent emission fingerprints
evidence_signal: PL shifts from about 2.48 to 2.70 eV while absorption stays near 3.8 eV, and measured anisotropy closely matches theory.
watch_item: The conclusions rely on nanocrystal composition control and model-based interpretation of STE behavior, so extending the results to other morphologies or operating conditions may require additional validation.
paper_title: Composition-controlled optical fingerprints and anisotropy of self-trapped excitons in double perovskites
